blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 1.18
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 1.18

blocks.text: लोकानन्दः समाधिसुखम्
blocks.directed: [slowly] लोकानन्दः समाधिसुखम्

blocks.text: Lokānandaḥ samādhisukham.
blocks.directed: Lokānandaḥ samādhisukham.

blocks.text: The bliss of the world is the happiness of samādhi.
blocks.directed: The bliss of the world is the happiness of samādhi.

blocks.text: The Entire World Has Become Your Meditation.
blocks.directed: The Entire World Has Become Your Meditation.

blocks.text: Oh, this is beautiful.
blocks.directed: Oh, this is beautiful.

blocks.text: Consider what many people imagine meditation to be.
blocks.directed: Consider what many people imagine meditation to be.

blocks.text: You sit down.
blocks.directed: You sit down.

blocks.text: Close your eyes.
blocks.directed: Close your eyes.

blocks.text: Withdraw from the horrible noisy world.
blocks.directed: Withdraw from the horrible noisy world.

blocks.text: Eventually, if you’re lucky, you get a special experience of peacefulness.
blocks.directed: Eventually, if you’re lucky, you get a special experience of peacefulness.

blocks.text: Then somebody starts drilling next door.
blocks.directed: Then somebody starts drilling next door.

blocks.text: And your enlightenment has been cancelled.
blocks.directed: And your enlightenment has been cancelled.

blocks.text: The neighbour’s power tools have defeated the Absolute.
blocks.directed: The neighbour’s power tools have defeated the Absolute.

blocks.text: A tragic outcome.
blocks.directed: A tragic outcome.

blocks.text: But Vasugupta is describing something more radical.
blocks.directed: But Vasugupta is describing something more radical.

blocks.text: Loka — the world, understood through the field of knowable objects and their experiencers.
blocks.directed: Loka — the world, understood through the field of knowable objects and their experiencers.

blocks.text: Ānanda — bliss.
blocks.directed: Ānanda — bliss.

blocks.text: Samādhi — absorption, integration, collectedness.
blocks.directed: Samādhi — absorption, integration, collectedness.

blocks.text: Sukha — happiness or delight.
blocks.directed: Sukha — happiness or delight.

blocks.text: For the yogi established in recognition, the very appearance of the world is inseparable from the delight of conscious reality.
blocks.directed: For the yogi established in recognition, the very appearance of the world is inseparable from the delight of conscious reality.

blocks.text: This doesn’t mean every worldly event becomes conventionally pleasant.
blocks.directed: This doesn’t mean every worldly event becomes conventionally pleasant.

blocks.text: Pain can still be pain.
blocks.directed: Pain can still be pain.

blocks.text: Loss can still be loss.
blocks.directed: Loss can still be loss.

blocks.text: The claim is that the underlying conscious reality is not separated from its manifestations by the ordinary division between meditation and daily life.
blocks.directed: The claim is that the underlying conscious reality is not separated from its manifestations by the ordinary division between meditation and daily life.

blocks.text: The yogi doesn’t necessarily have to escape the world to recover their fundamental nature.
blocks.directed: The yogi doesn’t necessarily have to escape the world to recover their fundamental nature.

blocks.text: The world itself becomes an occasion for recognition.
blocks.directed: The world itself becomes an occasion for recognition.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja connects this to resting in the position of the perceiver while the relation between experiencer and experienced remains manifest. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja connects this to resting in the position of the perceiver while the relation between experiencer and experienced remains manifest. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: Imagine sitting beside a river.
blocks.directed: Imagine sitting beside a river.

blocks.text: A bird calls.
blocks.directed: A bird calls.

blocks.text: The water moves.
blocks.directed: The water moves.

blocks.text: The air touches your skin.
blocks.directed: The air touches your skin.

blocks.text: A thought appears.
blocks.directed: A thought appears.

blocks.text: Normally, you might interpret these as separate things happening to a particular individual.
blocks.directed: Normally, you might interpret these as separate things happening to a particular individual.

blocks.text: But in the nondual recognition described here, their entire manifestation is apprehended within the indivisible reality of consciousness.
blocks.directed: But in the nondual recognition described here, their entire manifestation is apprehended within the indivisible reality of consciousness.

blocks.text: The river is not merely an obstruction to meditation.
blocks.directed: The river is not merely an obstruction to meditation.

blocks.text: The bird is not interrupting your spiritual attainment.
blocks.directed: The bird is not interrupting your spiritual attainment.

blocks.text: The world is not an unfortunate distraction from Śiva.
blocks.directed: The world is not an unfortunate distraction from Śiva.

blocks.text: It is Śiva’s own manifestation.
blocks.directed: It is Śiva’s own manifestation.

blocks.text: This is why Trika is so radically affirmative.
blocks.directed: This is why Trika is so radically affirmative.

blocks.text: It is not primarily trying to get rid of existence.
blocks.directed: It is not primarily trying to get rid of existence.

blocks.text: It is trying to recognise its deepest nature.
blocks.directed: It is trying to recognise its deepest nature.

blocks.text: And now we arrive at a rather unexpected turn.
blocks.directed: And now we arrive at a rather unexpected turn.

blocks.text: Because Vasugupta is about to start talking about supernatural powers.
blocks.directed: Because Vasugupta is about to start talking about supernatural powers.

blocks.text: Naturally.
blocks.directed: Naturally.
